title: Data Literacy
description: Grain, types, tidy tables, and questions a dataset can and cannot answer.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can state the grain of a row in one sentence, mark a column as a variable or a value, and name one question the table cannot answer — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can reshape a messy table into tidy form in versioned code, define missing values instead of silently filling them, and write the analysis question before the first insight heading.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently decide which questions a dataset can and cannot answer from grain and types, keep a dead-end in the repo, and change one assumption live and update the claim.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a wrong conclusion as a grain, type or tidy-form mistake, cite the row definition that was violated, and produce a schema note another analyst can apply to a new file.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's schema or EDA, name a question the grain cannot support (or a column treated as both variable and value), and teach how to read grain on an unfamiliar table.
